title: Before and after: did the new way of working work?
objective: Learners see the same rollout three ways (a slope per team, each team's change with its 95 % range, and the cohorts lined up by months since adoption) and learn why a leader should lead with the pooled change and its range, show every team's slope, and use the cohort grid to answer "was it just one good team?"

recommended.why: A slope chart is two columns and a line per team; D3 draws it exactly and lets the lines appear one by one and recolour when the ranges arrive.

alternative.why: The slope shows direction for every team; the dot plot with ranges shows which changes are real at this sample size. Which one goes on the first slide, and which one answers the sceptic?

assumptions: Teams, baselines and measurements are seeded synthetic numbers; the method, the metric (cycle time in days) and the teams are fictional
Each team's true improvement is the effect size plus a little team-to-team variation; measurements vary by 25 % around the truth, so a mean of n measurements has a standard error of 25 % / √n
The 95 % range of a change is ± 1.96 × √2 × standard error, expressed as a share of the before mean
Teams adopt in a staggered rollout over six months; the adoption month gets half the effect, the following months the full effect
The cohort grid averages the % change against baseline for the teams that adopted in the same month, by months since adoption
Playback: five scenes over about 21 s (before, after, ranges, cohorts, so what)
units: change: percent of the before mean, negative is better
sample size: measurements per team per period
months: calendar months of the rollout
checkDescription: Each team's change, margin and flags follow from its means; standard errors scale with 1/√n; the pooled change lies within three of its margins of the stated effect; every team sits in exactly one rollout cohort; cells before adoption average near zero and cells after it are negative when the effect is positive.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the measurements per team to 5 before you play. How many teams will clear zero on their own, and will any look worse?
learnerPrompts.explain: With the true improvement at 0 %, some teams still show a change. Explain to a sponsor why the cohort grid is the honest picture here.
